title: One switcher drives every screen
body: Location can be changed from any page that links to the same switcher. Data for all locations shows as a widget on the home page.

title: Settings moves to the left
body: Android typically launches a settings menu from the top left instead of iOS' top right position.

title: Widgets open full pages
body: Tapping a card pushes a page over the tab bar rather than a sheet. Earnings and shiftmates need room for detail, and a page keeps a back button. This allows progressive disclosure and keeps clutter to a minimum.

title: Shiftmates (proposed)
body: Data from Alvin and real-world users show that employees care about who they're working with. Let's make it a moment of mini-delight to see your fellow workers before your shift.

title: Employees use the clock regularly
body: We promote the timeclock to a delightful, always-available accessory bar that gives quick options for breaks and shift status.

title: Today at a glance
body: One card, three lenses: people, sales and foot traffic, each against plan by hour. It replaces three separate reports.

title: The main action is a button, not a menu
body: On Android each tab has one floating action: clock in on Home for employees, add shift, new message. iOS tucks the same actions into toolbar menus.

title: Split nav, labeled
body: Tabs sit together on the left and the assistant stands alone on the right. Employees have no assistant, so their tabs spread evenly across the bottom

title: All Locations
body: Multiple locations sees a single card that combines data across all locations, similar to the top section that exists for multi-location users today.

title: Settings
body: Remove the More tab bar option. Combine Profile, options, and settings into a single area with better information hierarchy.

title: All locations widget
body: Users who run multiple locations get an overview and a list they can tap into each store for more detail.

title: Requests
body: Requests moves to a first-class button in the toolbar because it's accessed often. Burying it also buries the notification badge so owners miss genuinely urgent requests.

title: Earnings promoted as quick display
body: Earnings used to tap into the Money screen. It still will, but shows clear information that may prevent the need to even tap further in.

title: Time off balance
body: Previously linked to a very simple full page that didn't need to be a full page. We can show that information right here (and still have a full page version if needed)

title: Settings (old)
body: Settings data used to be buried one level too deep, requiring a separate tap. At only 4 options, we should move it to the main area, especially after better reorganization.

title: Features and Growth
body: Three list items in the "More" menu were sales options disguised as settings. I pulled them out while keeping them accessible.

title: Untangling Profile
body: Previously Profile was a combination of user data, some public, some private. This treatment allows us to organize and highlight the most important things.

title: Pin Card
body: We can use the PIN that used to live further down the page as an opportunity to add interest and branding for businesses.

title: Praise gets more view
body: Move shoutouts to a more visible spot, along with Achievements for better feature adoption.
